areas.title: Scanning real projects
areas.description: Running the real command line against pinned example projects and comparing the entire result with a recorded one.

areas.title: Dependency graphs
areas.description: Working out which packages a project depends on, and how each one got there.

areas.title: Policy decisions
areas.description: Deciding what counts as a problem: licences, vulnerabilities, baselines, and packages that change where they come from.

areas.title: Reachability
areas.description: Judging whether a vulnerable package is actually used by the code that depends on it.

areas.title: Upgrade guidance
areas.description: The fixes Bomly recommends, worked out without changing anything in your project.

areas.title: Comparing two scans
areas.description: Telling what genuinely changed between two scans, and what only looks new.

areas.title: Other scan targets
areas.description: Scanning things that are not a local source tree, such as container images.

areas.title: SBOM compatibility
areas.description: Reading SBOM documents other tools produce, and writing ones they accept.

areas.title: Running everywhere
areas.description: Behaving the same on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and building for every processor a release supports.

areas.title: Handling broken input
areas.description: Reading damaged or hostile project, configuration, and SBOM files without crashing.

areas.title: Speed and repeatability
areas.description: How long a repeated scan takes, and whether it returns the same answer every time.

areas.title: What you download
areas.description: Whether the published files are complete, unaltered, and signed by this project's release pipeline.

areas.title: Installing it
areas.description: Whether the documented ways of installing this release actually work.

areas.title: This report itself
areas.description: The catalog and contracts the report is built from, and the check that keeps them honest.

checks.title: Assurance catalog is valid
checks.description: Validates this catalog and confirms every fixture and expected-result file it points at exists.
checks.summary: The assurance catalog is valid and every fixture and expected-result file it names exists.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: The assurance catalog is valid and every fixture and expected-result file it names exists.

proves: Every claim in this report points at a real check and at files that are present in this release's source.
limitations: A valid catalog says the paperwork is consistent; the checks themselves decide whether the software works.

checks.title: Release binaries build for every target
checks.description: Cross-compiles the full and lite binaries for every supported operating system and processor from the same source tree.
checks.summary: All 12 release binaries built: full and lite for Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: All 12 release binaries built: full and lite for Linux, macOS, and Windows on amd64 and arm64.

proves: The source tree compiles into both binaries for every Linux, macOS, and Windows target a release ships.
limitations: A successful build is not a test: it does not run the binary or check what it produces.

checks.title: Parsers survive malformed input
checks.description: Runs every registered Go fuzz target against the parsers that read untrusted project, configuration, baseline, SBOM, and plugin data.
checks.summary: 30 fuzz targets ran for 30s each against their seed corpus without finding a crash.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: 30 fuzz targets ran for 30s each against their seed corpus without finding a crash.

proves: Each registered parser handled its seed corpus and newly generated inputs without crashing during the time budget of this run.
limitations: Fuzzing explores a limited time budget. A clean run is evidence of robustness, not proof that no malformed input can cause a failure.
Parsers that are command-backed or handled entirely by the standard library are excluded and listed in test/assurance/PARSER_FUZZING.md.

checks.title: Install scripts install the release
checks.description: Runs the published install script on each operating system against this release and asks the installed binary for its version.

instances.name: macos
instances.summary: The published install script installed Bomly 0.28.0 on macOS and the binary reported: bomly 0.28.0

instances.name: ubuntu
instances.summary: The published install script installed Bomly 0.28.0 on Linux and the binary reported: bomly 0.28.0

instances.name: windows
instances.summary: The published install script installed Bomly 0.28.0 on Windows and the binary reported: bomly 0.28.0

proves: The documented one-line install works on Linux, macOS, and Windows for this exact release, and the installed binary reports this version.
limitations: This installs into a temporary directory on a clean runner. It does not cover every shell, proxy, or locked-down corporate environment.

checks.title: Repeated scan speed and stability
checks.description: Runs the same offline scan with the released binary several times with a cold cache and several times with a warm cache, and records timing, memory, and output stability.
checks.summary: canonical-sbom-scan completed 5 samples per cache mode with identical normalized output (cold median 21 ms, warm median 21 ms).

instances.name: default
instances.summary: canonical-sbom-scan completed 5 samples per cache mode with identical normalized output (cold median 21 ms, warm median 21 ms).

proves: Repeated runs of the same scan produced identical normalized output, and the recorded timings show how long that scan took on this machine.
limitations: Timing and memory are observations from one CI machine, not limits. Comparing them across releases is only meaningful because the case and the machine class stay the same.

checks.title: Published files download and match
checks.description: Downloads every published file from its public URL, without credentials, verifies the signature on the published checksum list, and checks each file against it.
checks.summary: All 23 published files downloaded from their public URLs without credentials and match the signed checksum list.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: All 23 published files downloaded from their public URLs without credentials and match the signed checksum list.

proves: Every file a user downloads from the public release page is present, reachable without credentials, and matches a checksum list signed by this repository's release workflow.
limitations: This checks availability and integrity at one moment from one network location.
It confirms the published files match the signed list; it does not re-check the provenance attestation, which is verified before publication.
Whether each archive contains a working binary is checked separately, against the draft release and by the install scripts.

checks.title: Every release file is attached
checks.description: Compares the files attached to the draft release against the full list a release is required to ship.
checks.summary: 22 of 23 expected release assets are attached.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: 22 of 23 expected release assets are attached.

proves: The release carries an archive for every supported platform, both binaries, every Linux package format, the checksum list, its signature, and the provenance file.
limitations: This counts files. Whether each archive contains a working binary is checked separately.

checks.title: Released binaries report this version
checks.description: Extracts the archives built for each operating system and runs the binaries inside them.
proves: Both the full and lite binaries start on Linux, macOS, and Windows and report the version that is being released.
limitations: Only the architecture of the CI runner is executed for each operating system; other architectures are verified by checksum and build only.

checks.title: Release files match their checksums
checks.description: Hashes every release file each platform downloads and compares it with the published SHA256SUMS list.

instances.name: darwin-arm64
instances.summary: 2 downloaded assets match SHA256SUMS, which lists 20 files.

instances.name: linux-amd64
instances.summary: 20 downloaded assets match SHA256SUMS, which lists 20 files.

instances.name: windows-amd64
instances.summary: 2 downloaded assets match SHA256SUMS, which lists 20 files.

proves: Every file the release ships hashes to exactly the value recorded in the checksum list, and the list covers every file.
limitations: Checksums prove the files were not altered after they were built; the signature and provenance checks prove who built them.

checks.title: Build provenance verifies
checks.description: Verifies the SLSA build provenance attached to the release with slsa-verifier.
checks.summary: slsa-verifier could not verify the build provenance attached to this release.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: slsa-verifier could not verify the build provenance attached to this release.

proves: The release archives were produced by this repository's tagged release workflow, as recorded in signed build provenance.
limitations: Provenance describes how and where the files were built. It does not review what the source code does.

checks.title: Checksum list is signed
checks.description: Verifies the Sigstore signature over the release checksum list with cosign.
checks.summary: The checksum list carries a valid Sigstore signature issued to this repository's release workflow.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: The checksum list carries a valid Sigstore signature issued to this repository's release workflow.

proves: The checksum list carries a valid Sigstore signature issued to this repository's release workflow, so the checksums themselves can be trusted.
limitations: The signature covers the checksum list. Individual files are tied to it through their checksums.

checks.title: The released binary scans real projects
checks.description: Runs scan, diff, and explain with the binary from the published release against pinned example repositories and checks the results against the same golden files the source-tree smoke tests use.
proves: The binary users actually download produces the same dependency graphs as the source tree it was built from.
limitations: A representative subset of ecosystems runs against the released binary; the full ecosystem matrix runs on the source tree before the release is tagged.

checks.title: Official validators accept our SBOMs
checks.description: Generates SPDX 2.3 and CycloneDX 1.7 documents with the released binary — one pair from a single input and one pair merged from two source documents — and validates all four with checksum-pinned official SPDX and CycloneDX tools.
checks.summary: SBOM interoperability run failed: validator java failed with exit 1.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: SBOM interoperability run failed: validator java failed with exit 1.

proves: The SBOM documents this release writes are accepted by the official SPDX and CycloneDX validators, at the exact validator versions recorded in the result.
A document merged from two sources states its own identity and links both sources, rather than adopting one of them.
limitations: Validators check that a document is well formed against its specification. They do not check that every receiving tool interprets it the same way.
The merge case uses two checked-in fixtures; it does not cover every combination of source formats.

checks.title: End-to-end scans of real projects
checks.description: Runs scan, diff, and explain against pinned public repositories, one slice per ecosystem, and compares the whole result with checked-in golden files.
proves: For every supported ecosystem, the command line produces exactly the dependency graph, policy result, and output shape recorded in the golden files.
limitations: Golden files pin one revision of one example project per ecosystem. They do not cover every project layout or every version of a package manager.
Cases that reach live advisory services can change when upstream data changes.

checks.title: Unit tests pass on every platform
checks.description: Runs the full Go unit test suite twice on Linux, macOS, and Windows, so a pass is never a single lucky run.

instances.name: macos-latest
instances.summary: The complete Go test suite passed twice on macOS/ARM64, with no reused results.

instances.name: ubuntu-latest
instances.summary: The complete Go test suite passed twice on Linux/X64, with no reused results.

instances.name: windows-latest
instances.summary: The complete Go test suite passed twice on Windows/X64, with no reused results.

proves: Every unit test passes on all three supported operating systems, twice in a row, so a pass is not a one-off.
limitations: Unit tests run in process against fixtures. They do not download repositories or call external services.

checks.title: Java detector tests are stable
checks.description: Runs the Gradle, Maven, and sbt detector test suites ten times, because build-tool-backed detectors are where intermittent failures have actually appeared.
checks.summary: The Gradle, Maven, and sbt detector suites passed ten times in a row.

instances.name: default
instances.summary: The Gradle, Maven, and sbt detector suites passed ten times in a row.

proves: The build-tool-backed Java detector suites passed ten consecutive times.
limitations: This exercises the detectors against local fixtures with the toolchain installed on the runner.

evidence.title: Finding baseline lifecycle
evidence.description: Records a package finding in a project baseline, then scans again and compares the whole result with a recorded one.
proves: A project baseline can keep a denied package finding visible with suppressed policy status.
limitations: The local matcher fixture is deterministic but does not measure advisory freshness.

evidence.title: Container package inventory
evidence.description: Scans a public container image and compares the operating-system packages found with a recorded inventory.
proves: Bomly can inventory the operating-system packages in the checked Alpine image.
limitations: The upstream image tag can move; the checked-in golden is a snapshot, not an immutable image claim.

evidence.title: Visible detector fallback
evidence.description: Forces a detector to fall back to a second technique and checks that the result says so instead of hiding it.
proves: A detector fallback preserves its origin and produces a typed degraded-coverage warning.
limitations: The synthetic detector case proves orchestration behavior, not the fidelity of every concrete fallback.

evidence.title: Bun lockfile graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned Bun example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The native Bun detector preserves the package inventory and dependency placement represented by the pinned lockfile.
limitations: This is one Bun lockfile shape and does not prove behavior for every historical Bun format.

evidence.title: Go module graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned Go example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The Go detector resolves a build-tool-backed module graph for the pinned repository.
limitations: The result depends on a compatible Go toolchain and the evidence available from that toolchain.

evidence.title: Maven dependency graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned Maven example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The Maven detector resolves a build-tool-backed dependency graph for the pinned repository.
limitations: Artifact resolution depends on Maven repositories and a compatible Java and Maven installation.

evidence.title: npm lockfile graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned npm example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The npm detector preserves lockfile package inventory, versions, scopes, and dependency placement.
limitations: This case covers the lockfile versions present in one pinned repository.

evidence.title: pnpm lockfile graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned pnpm example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The pnpm detector preserves lockfile package inventory and dependency placement.
limitations: This case does not cover every pnpm lockfile generation.

evidence.title: Python requirements graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned Python example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The pip detector reads the pinned requirements lock and preserves the resolved Python package graph.
limitations: Unpinned requirements and environment inspection have different fidelity and are not proven by this case.

evidence.title: Yarn lockfile graph
evidence.description: Scans a pinned Yarn example project and compares the whole dependency graph with a recorded one.
proves: The Yarn detector preserves package inventory and dependency placement represented by the pinned lockfile.
limitations: This case covers one Yarn lockfile family; fallback behavior is documented separately.

evidence.title: Complex and invalid SPDX policy
evidence.description: Evaluates licence policy against a matrix of SPDX expressions, including combined, nested, exception, custom, and invalid ones.
proves: The license auditor evaluates AND, OR, nested, exception, custom-reference, and invalid SPDX expressions under allow and deny policy.
limitations: The tests prove policy evaluation after license data is present; they do not prove the accuracy of every upstream license source.

evidence.title: Risk that persists across a version change
evidence.description: Compares two scans across a package version change and checks how a finding that survives the change is classified.
proves: A vulnerability or license finding that remains across a package version change is classified as persisted instead of one resolved and one introduced finding.
limitations: Persistence uses the canonical package-finding identity; a genuinely different advisory or rule remains a distinct finding.

evidence.title: Go vulnerability reachability
evidence.description: Analyses a pinned Go project and checks the reachability evidence attached to each matched vulnerability.
proves: The Go analyzer attaches named analyzer, tier, status, and reason evidence to matched vulnerabilities.
limitations: Advisories come from live services and may change; an unreachable result is not proof that a package is safe.

evidence.title: Java package reachability
evidence.description: Analyses a pinned Java project and checks the reachability evidence attached to each matched vulnerability.
proves: The Java analyzer separates package-reachable and package-unreachable vulnerability evidence.
limitations: This is package-tier evidence, not symbol-level proof, and live advisory results may change.

evidence.title: JavaScript package reachability
evidence.description: Analyses a pinned JavaScript project and checks the reachability evidence attached to each matched vulnerability.
proves: The JavaScript analyzer separates package-reachable and package-unreachable vulnerability evidence.
limitations: This is package-tier evidence, dynamic loading can reduce confidence, and live advisory results may change.

evidence.title: Python package reachability
evidence.description: Analyses a pinned Python project and checks the reachability evidence attached to each matched vulnerability.
proves: The Python analyzer separates package-reachable and package-unreachable vulnerability evidence.
limitations: This is package-tier evidence, reflective imports can reduce confidence, and live advisory results may change.

evidence.title: Canonical read-only remediation guidance
evidence.description: Derives upgrade guidance for a set of findings and checks the fix status, versions, and per-occurrence advice it produces.
proves: One central component derives fix status, recommended versions, occurrence actions, and detector advice without applying changes.
limitations: Suggestions are read-only evidence and are not guaranteed to work in every checkout.

evidence.title: CycloneDX 1.6 ingestion
evidence.description: Reads a checked-in CycloneDX document and compares the dependency graph it produces with a recorded one.
proves: Bomly ingests the checked CycloneDX 1.6 dependency graph.
limitations: The fixture covers one document shape and does not imply lossless conversion from every producer.

evidence.title: SPDX 2.3 ingestion
evidence.description: Reads a checked-in SPDX document and compares the dependency graph it produces with a recorded one.
proves: Bomly ingests the checked SPDX 2.3 dependency graph.
limitations: The fixture covers one document shape and does not imply lossless conversion from every producer.

evidence.title: Registry-to-Git source-change review
evidence.description: Compares two scans of the same project where one package moved from a registry to a Git source, and checks how that is flagged.
proves: Diff marks a same-version registry-to-Git move for review and the package auditor can fail it when source-change policy is enabled.
limitations: A source change is a review signal, not proof of malicious intent, and unknown source evidence cannot be classified.

evidence.title: Vulnerability policy constraints
evidence.description: Evaluates vulnerability policy against a matrix of severities, reachability tiers, known exploitation, and advisory allowlists.
proves: The vulnerability auditor composes severity, reachability, known exploitation, and advisory allowlists with the documented repeated-constraint behavior.
limitations: Policy can only evaluate vulnerability, reachability, and exploitation evidence that is present in the registry.
